violations.description: Hardcoded database credential in source code
violations.recommendation: Migrate database credentials to environment variables or a secret management vault (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).

violations.evidence: on: [pull_request_target] followed by checkout of untrusted head branch
violations.recommendation: Use the standard 'pull_request' trigger for untrusted forks or restrict checkout to the base repository to prevent workflow PWN exploitation.

violations.description: Missing explicit least-privilege permissions in GitHub Actions workflow
violations.evidence: No top-level 'permissions:' block defined, granting default read/write access to GITHUB_TOKEN
violations.recommendation: Define top-level 'permissions: read-all' or specify minimal required scopes (e.g. contents: read) to follow least-privilege principles.

violations.description: Unpinned production dependencies allowing wildcard breaking changes
violations.evidence: flask>=2.0.* and requests specified without upper bounds or exact lock
violations.recommendation: Pin dependency versions or adopt a lockfile system (e.g. poetry.lock, pip-tools) for deterministic, reproducible builds.

violations.description: OS-generated metadata file tracked in git repository
violations.evidence: Tracked binary file '.DS_Store' present in repository index
violations.recommendation: Remove '.DS_Store' from git tracking using 'git rm --cached .DS_Store' and add it to the project '.gitignore'.

violations.description: Repository lacks automated test suite or test discovery directory
violations.evidence: No tests/ directory, test_*.py, or *_test.py files detected in repository structure
violations.recommendation: Establish a tests/ suite with pytest and configure automated test execution in CI workflows.
Parameterize paths via environment variables or make them relative to project root.
